nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space, $A \subseteq E$ and $y \in E$. Then $y$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$ if and only if $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$ for every $x \in A$.
nodes.title: Membership in the polar

nodes.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the closed unit ball $\{x \in E : \|x\| \le 1\}$ is the closed unit ball itself.
nodes.title: The closed unit ball is self-polar

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the polar of the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is the set of all $y$ with $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$ for every $x$ in the cube, is the closed $\ell^1$ unit ball $\{y \in \mathbb{R}^n : \sum_i |y_i| \le 1\}$.
nodes.title: The polar of the cube is the $\ell^1$ unit ball

nodes.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the empty set is all of $E$, since the defining condition is vacuous.
nodes.title: Polar of the empty set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, let $f : E \to F$ be a linear map with adjoint $f^* : F \to E$, and let $K \subseteq E$. Writing $S^\circ$ for the polar of a set $S$, we have $(f(K))^\circ = (f^*)^{-1}(K^\circ)$, that is, $y \in F$ lies in the polar of $f(K)$ if and only if $f^*(y)$ lies in the polar of $K$.
nodes.title: Polar of a linear image

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a real inner product space. If $A \subseteq B$, then the polar $B^\circ$ of $B$ is contained in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$.
nodes.title: The polar reverses inclusion

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space. The polar of a set $A \subseteq E$ is the set $A^\circ = \{y \in E : \langle x, y \rangle \le 1 \text{ for all } x \in A\}$. This uses the one-sided bound $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$, not $|\langle x, y \rangle| \le 1$.
nodes.title: Polar of a set

nodes.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, for every set $A \subseteq E$ the origin $0$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$, since $\langle x, 0 \rangle = 0 \le 1$ for every $x \in A$.
nodes.title: The origin lies in every polar
